measured: Read on 2026-10-08 from what LibreChat's own driver sent a MongoDB server, not from its source alone, in two readings; 1081 command documents in all. LibreChat at the commit below was installed and built by its own scripts and started against MongoDB Community 7.0.16 with the server's profiler recording every operation from before the application's first connection. First reading: a standalone server, driven by HTTP through boot, registration, sign-in, the requests of a first page, sign-out and a second sign-in. Second reading: attached to a World with the OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini twins and a World-managed server as a one-member replica set (the cookbook's configuration), driven by HTTP through boot, registration, sign-in, one chat turn to each provider read to its final event, the conversation list, and each conversation reopened with its messages. Each row below is one command on one collection, with how often and in which phases it was sent; its evidence is the line of LibreChat that makes the collection LibreChat's: the registration of its mongoose model (mongoose issues create and createIndexes from that registration, and every query on the model is built by mongoose from calls on it), or, for a collection used without a model, the line that names it. The call site of each individual query was not traced. No command of either reading carried a transaction, on the replica set where one was available (the instrument was shown a transaction and reported it). Ruled out and not in this demand: everything LibreChat does only when an integration is switched on (social sign-in, file storage, search, MCP servers, whose authority read starts a snapshot transaction), and the server's own profiling collection. Counts understate a command repeated with no effect: the server's profiler does not record a second create or createIndexes that changes nothing (asked of the server).
